_note: The 26 SWD clubs. Read by /club-info and the app. lat/lng are the club green. 'id' is the club's permanent id (app follows and links use it; never change it). 'aliases' lists other spellings used for this club as a tournament venue in events-data.json.

clubs.name: Beverly Hills
clubs.summary: Fun, challenging club at Roxbury Park with regular weekend and Wednesday bowls.
clubs.details: Located at Roxbury Park, 401 S. Roxbury Dr., Beverly Hills. The club presents an exceptional sport that is fun and challenging, with excellent facilities and play at all skill levels. Beverly Hills bowls regularly on Saturday and Sunday mornings at 10:00 AM and Wednesdays at noon.

clubs.name: Cambria
clubs.summary: Central Coast club with an artificial turf green and a welcoming visitor culture.
clubs.details: Cambria Lawn Bowls Green is located on California’s Central Coast, established in 1968. The green was refurbished in 2019, and the club bowls several times a week while welcoming visitors and people interested in learning about bowls.

clubs.name: Casta del Sol
clubs.summary: Private community club that sponsors tournament play during the year.
clubs.details: Casta del Sol Lawn Bowling Club is a private club open to residents of the community. The club sponsors tournament play during the year.

clubs.name: Coronado
clubs.summary: Historic club with a world-class artificial green next to the library and high school.
clubs.details: The Coronado Lawn Bowling Club started in 1935. The original grass green was replaced with a new artificial green dedicated in 2010 at 1019 Seventh St. (7th and D Ave). The club holds a permit to use the green, which is also open to the public.

clubs.name: Friendly Valley
clubs.summary: Resident-only club formed in 1966.
clubs.details: Formed in 1966 by residents of the Friendly Valley community in Santa Clarita. It is a private club open to residents only.

clubs.name: Hemet-Joslyn
clubs.summary: Longstanding park-based club with a snowbird and year-round player community.
clubs.details: The first president was elected in 1976, the greens were dedicated in 1977, the clubhouse was completed in 1989, and the greens were amended in 1992 for tournament length. Located at Gibbel Park in Hemet. Open Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

clubs.name: Hermosa Beach
clubs.summary: Longtime South Bay club, founded in 1936 and welcoming to new bowlers.
clubs.details: The Hermosa Beach Lawn Bowling Club was founded in 1936 and is a member of the Southwest Bowls Division. The club welcomes visitors and new players.

clubs.name: Holmby Park
clubs.summary: Diverse Los Angeles club in a beautiful park setting with easy parking.
clubs.details: Holmby Park Lawn Bowling Club, founded in 1927, is situated in one of the most beautiful parks in Los Angeles at 646 Comstock Avenue. It is open to all who can pass a simple lawn bowling test and highlights a diverse membership across ages and backgrounds.

clubs.name: Laguna Beach
clubs.summary: Iconic ocean-view club in Heisler Park and one of the largest in the USA.
clubs.details: Established in 1931 and situated in Heisler Park overlooking the Pacific. Members enjoy both social and tournament bowls, plus complimentary lessons in basics, strategy, etiquette, and team games.

clubs.name: Laguna Woods
clubs.summary: Private community club known for hosting divisional and national tournaments.
clubs.details: Laguna Woods is a private club in the Laguna Woods Village community, established in 1966. The club often hosts divisional and national tournaments, including major events. The greens are synthetic.

clubs.name: Long Beach
clubs.summary: Large, development-focused club with strong social and competitive support.
clubs.details: Located at 1109 Federation Drive in Recreation Park, Long Beach emphasizes introducing new players to the game while also supporting members who want social play or higher-level competition. The club counts past national champions and international competitors among its membership.

clubs.name: MacKenzie Park
clubs.summary: Santa Barbara club with two greens, clubhouse facilities, and free introductory lessons.
clubs.details: Located in upper MacKenzie Park in Santa Barbara. The club is open year-round and offers free, no-obligation lessons, visitor access, and a full facility including clubhouse, kitchen, and lockers.

clubs.name: Newport Harbor
clubs.summary: Beautiful, major club with strong social and competitive bowling opportunities.
clubs.details: Nestled at 1550 Crown Drive North in Corona del Mar, Newport Harbor is one of the largest and most beautiful lawn bowling clubs in the United States. Members enjoy organized social and competitive bowling throughout the week.

clubs.name: Oaks North
clubs.summary: Community-center club in Rancho Bernardo that often hosts local and divisional tournaments.
clubs.details: Oaks North is a club based at the Oaks North Community Center in Rancho Bernardo (San Diego), established in 1974. It often hosts local and divisional tournaments. The greens are synthetic.

clubs.name: Oxnard-Joslyn
clubs.summary: Senior-center-based club in Wilson Park with a central Oxnard location.
clubs.details: The club is part of the Oxnard Senior Center in Wilson Park, located downtown at 350 North “C” Street. It was founded through the efforts of Marcellus L. Joslyn.

clubs.name: Pasadena
clubs.summary: Oldest club in Southern California and a foundational club in California bowls history.
clubs.details: Established in 1921 at 275 S. Raymond Ave. in Central Park, Pasadena is described as the birthplace of California lawn bowling. The Pasadena Lawn Bowling & Croquet Club hosts the Rose Lawn Bowl each New Year’s Eve.

clubs.name: Pomona
clubs.summary: Active inland club with regular bowls, coaching, and social play.
clubs.details: Located at 451 East Arrow Highway in Pomona, the club offers regular bowling, coaching for new players, and social events throughout the year.

clubs.name: Redlands
clubs.summary: Historic inland club with active membership and regular bowls, including Rock and Bowl.
clubs.details: The club was formed in 1921 and moved to its current Sylvan Park location (411 N University St) in 1923. It offers robust membership, regular bowls, coaching, and Saturday evening Rock and Bowl.

clubs.name: Riverside
clubs.summary: Fairmount Park club welcoming visitors and new members.
clubs.details: Located in Fairmount Park at 4020 Bowling Green Drive, Riverside, the club is a member of the Southwest Division and welcomes visitors and new bowlers.

clubs.name: San Diego
clubs.summary: Historic Balboa Park club with strong national and international competitive pedigree.
clubs.details: An iconic member of Balboa Park, on the corner of El Prado and Balboa Drive, the San Diego Lawn Bowling Club was established in 1932 and features the only natural grass rink in San Diego. The club has produced numerous national and international champions.

clubs.name: Santa Ana
clubs.summary: Long-running Santiago Park club with public bowling hours and free lessons.
clubs.details: Santa Ana Lawn Bowling Club has been open continuously since 1938 at 510 E Memory Lane in Santiago Park. The club offers a membership program, free introductory lessons, and posted bowling schedules.

clubs.name: Santa Anita
clubs.summary: One of only two clubs in the United States with four greens, including lights for night bowling.
clubs.details: Santa Anita welcomes new members and notes that after only one or two lessons, players are ready for social bowling. The four greens are located at 405 S. Santa Anita Ave. in Arcadia County Park, and the club hosts the annual Southwest Open.

clubs.name: Santa Barbara
clubs.summary: Non-profit club with free introductory lessons, year-round use, and a strong community culture.
clubs.details: Santa Barbara Lawn Bowls Club, at 1216 De La Vina St., is a non-profit co-sponsored by the City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation. Visitors are welcome, introductory lessons are free, and facilities are available year-round.

clubs.name: Santa Monica
clubs.summary: Friendly club playing at Douglas Park, welcoming visitors and new bowlers.
clubs.details: The Santa Monica Lawn Bowls Club plays at Douglas Park in Santa Monica. The club offers social bowls and membership, and welcomes visitors and people who want to learn the game.

clubs.name: Sun City
clubs.summary: Long-established community club with varied bowling schedules and summer night bowling.
clubs.details: Organized in 1963 in the Del Webb retirement community of Sun City (Menifee), at 26850 Sun City Blvd. Members bowl several days a week, with night bowling in summer.

clubs.name: The Groves
clubs.summary: Private community club that often hosts divisional tournaments.
clubs.details: The Groves is a private club located in the gated Groves community at 5200 Irvine Blvd, Irvine. It often hosts divisional tournaments.
